title: Interest Days on Member Appeals to Out-of-Network Plans Paying Second — Insurance Coverage & Claims
content:
**Insurance Coverage & Claims — interest on member appeals to an out-of-network plan that pays second.** The second-plan member appeal's interest days turn on the plan's adjudication time, counted in calendar days between the claim's filing date and its denial date (the latest denial date on the claim), against the expected adjudication period of the coverage's payer class.

## Rule in three branches

- **Adjudication more than twice the expected period** — interest runs for every calendar day from the filing date to today.
- **More than the expected period but not more than twice it** — interest runs for the calendar days from the filing date to today less the expected adjudication days.
- **Otherwise** — no interest runs.

The member's interest is the net exposure times the member interest rate, divided by one hundred, times the interest days, divided by 365.

## Expected adjudication periods by payer class

| Payer class | Expected adjudication period (calendar days of filing) | More than this | More than twice this |
|---|---|---|---|
| Original Medicare Part B | 14 | 15 or more days | 29 or more days |
| Medicare Advantage Plan | 30 | 31 or more days | 61 or more days |
| Medicare Supplement Plan | 14 | 15 or more days | 29 or more days |
| Medicaid Managed Care Plan | 30 | 31 or more days | 61 or more days |
| TRICARE Prime and Select | 30 | 31 or more days | 61 or more days |
| Commercial In-Network Plan | 30 | 31 or more days | 61 or more days |
| Commercial Out-of-Network Plan | 45 | 46 or more days | 91 or more days |

## Hypothetical illustration (Commercial Out-of-Network Plan, expected period 45 days)

A claim filed 150 days ago and denied 100 days after filing: 100 is more than twice 45, so interest runs for all 150 days. Had it been denied 60 days after filing, interest would run for 150 less 45, that is 105 days; denied 45 days after filing, none.
